corrections: Two mechanisms are wrongly attributed. (1) It says qm agents 'emit reactions through a typed tool capped at 5 per turn'. In fact qm uses a text directive in the model reply ([[react: name @ ~id]]) that the Slack adapter parses with a regex and caps at 5. The cluster itself recommended a typed tool as an improvement over qm. Rephrase as 'qm: reply directive, max 5; recommend a typed tool for Verevon'. Inbound reactions reach the agent as a rendered '[Slack reaction] ...' text turn, not a typed {reaction, target_seq, by} object. qm revision entries target the Slack message ts, not a seq. (2) It says 'slack: role=toolbar per message with roving focus and a more-menu'. The role=toolbar evidence is GrokBot (index-Bo3NzkuN.js sand-message-hover-actions). Slack's records cover the rich clipboard and the native context menu only, and roving focus was not verified anywhere. Also: buzz 'soft-deleted events kept in audit' comes from VISION.md (DOC), not code. buzz's client-side permission has no admin branch; admin delete comes only from the Slack/Teams policy docs. qm has no edit or delete UI of its own; it ingests Slack edit/delete events. So qm's place in the 4-of-5 edit/delete count means 'handles edits made on its Slack surface', not 'offers edit/delete'.
caveats: qm reactions and edits are Slack-surface features (qm reuses Slack's reactions and edit events); there is no qm-native reactions table

corrections: The R-t1-10-02 mechanism (instance bound to one audience, memory with audience labels and membership epochs, subset rule, owner declassify) is written as reference practice, but it exists only in buzz's DRAFT design doc. The ifc-core crate is unused. Label it a proposal (DOC), not shipped behaviour, and do not make buzz the best source for a capability no reference ships. Treat qm as the best-in-class shipped implementation. GrokBot's 'runtime labelling of outbound Slack/Gmail/Outlook sends' is a remote-config (feature flag) schema with sampling rates. The connector list is supplied by the server, and the names Slack, Gmail and Outlook are not in the shipped schema (inference). It samples sends for labelling and review rather than blocking them. In R-t1-07-08, 'audience-safe disclosure 4 of 5 (table-stakes)' is overstated. Shipped audience intersection exists only in qm. Teams has review-then-share UX (strings plus DOC). Slack's model is 'agent reach equals the requester's reach' (DOC), which is weaker and different. buzz is the draft. Rephrase as a differentiator, 1 shipped plus 2 partial. The qm compaction 'tainted flag' is securityTainted, which marks prompt-injection or untrusted input, not audience. Audience safety comes from the summary label being the session scope. 'Derived content takes the maximum label of its sources' is a recommendation. Teams explicitly does not do this for AI output, and qm labels summaries with the session scope. For Teams knowledge scope, 'removal deletes derived knowledge, re-add starts from zero' and 'add requires membership' are DOC. The shipped strings show only that membership is required to remove a source.
